findings.evidence: The RPC converts a missing occurred_at to now and rejects only timestamps more than five minutes in the future. It never compares the transfer time with the source provider event or current entitlement authority. Transfer locks use revenuecat-transfer-user:* while ordinary renewal writes lock revenuecat-premium:<user>:<product>. A renewal can therefore update after the transfer reads the source but before its nested source revocation, after which the transfer overwrites the newer state using the stale pre-lock snapshot.
findings.impact: A delayed TRANSFER or renewal-versus-transfer interleaving can revoke or move a newer authoritative entitlement, violating the registered older-event and single-owner invariants.
findings.requiredResolution: Do not rewrite either deployed migration. Keep the webhook undeployed and add a separately reviewed forward-only correction that shares the Premium user/product lock domain, validates a non-null provider timestamp against authoritative state, and has deterministic delayed-event plus renewal-versus-transfer tests.

findings.evidence: The reconciliation report marks T3_INTEGRATION INTEGRATION_CLEAR and lists out_of_order coverage, but the fixture test only exercises resolveRevenueCatTransferUsers and static source ordering. It never invokes the webhook, RPC, or a renewal-versus-transfer schedule, and the 27-case pgTAP file has duplicate and rollback cases but no stale transfer or concurrent renewal case.
findings.impact: Fixture labels and source checks are being allowed to stand in for the missing atomic ordering proof, exactly the proof substitution the assurance contract requires rejecting.
findings.requiredResolution: Set T3_INTEGRATION to BLOCKED_INTERNAL until a deterministic database ordering/interleaving test passes. Keep fixture-corpus existence classified as T1 source evidence only.
